transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... I came in because... well, things have been a little difficult lately. I try so hard to keep the peace, I really do, but... it's my in-laws. We've been arguing, which I know happens in every family, but... I don't want you to think poorly of me for saying this, but it's not just a normal disagreement anymore. 

I... well, I realized that they are actually using the altar at church, and the parish committee, to try and push me out. They want to make everyone forget all the things I’ve done for this family over the years. I know how that might sound, and I hope you don't think I'm just being a complainer... but it's what they're doing. Is it okay that I'm sharing this with you? I just didn't know who else to talk to.
Do you have any proof that your in-laws are using the church and parish committee against you?

Proof? Oh, dear... I... I really hope you don't think I'm just making things up. I try so hard to see the good in everyone, I really do. I don't want to sound like a difficult person. 

But... well, I don't have a letter or a recording or anything concrete like that to show you. It's just... I just know it. You can feel it, you know? It's like I was saying, it's not just regular arguing with me anymore. I can see how they act with the parish committee, and the things they do up at the altar... they're using it to push me out. They want to make everyone completely forget all the things I’ve done for this family over the years. I've sacrificed so much for them, and now it's like they're trying to erase me from the church entirely. 

I know it sounds terrible to say out loud, and I'm so sorry if I sound foolish or vindictive... I really don't want to be a bother. But a person just knows when something like that is happening to them, don't they? Does that make sense to you, Doctor?
Do you think your in-laws would be doing these things against you if you weren't in the picture?

Oh... um, well, no, I don't think they would. I really hope I don't sound self-centered saying this—I promise I'm not trying to make everything about me, and I don't want you to think I'm full of myself. 

But... it really is directed at me. Like I was trying to explain before, they are specifically using the parish committee and the altar to push *me* out. If I weren't in the picture, they wouldn't need to go to such lengths to make everyone forget all the things I've done for this family over the years. It's... it's about erasing my place here, completely. 

I feel just terrible talking about my own family this way, I really do. It goes against everything I believe in to speak ill of them, and it embarrasses me to even have to bring it up. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope you don't think I'm just being unreasonable or vain.
Do you think your in-laws are plotting against you specifically, or is it just that you disagree with their actions?

Oh... um, well... I really don't want to sound like one of those people who thinks everyone is out to get them. I try so hard to be agreeable and to see the other side of things, I really do. I hope you believe me when I say that. 

But... it's not just a simple disagreement. I wish it were, I really do. It would be so much easier if we just didn't see eye-to-eye on things. But like I was saying before... I came in today because I finally realized that they aren't just arguing with me anymore. They are actually plotting, using the altar and the parish committee, specifically to push me out. They want to make sure everyone completely forgets all the sacrifices I've made for this family. 

It sounds so dramatic when I say it out loud, and I'm so sorry if it makes me seem paranoid or... or crazy. I really don't want you to think poorly of me. But it's just what's happening. Do you... do you think it's wrong of me to feel this way, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this right.
Do you think others can see what your in-laws are doing to you, or do you feel like you're the only one who notices?

Oh... well, I... I really don't want to make it sound like I'm trying to turn people against them or anything. I always try to keep family matters private, you know? I'd hate for you to think I'm gossiping or trying to cause a scene at the church. 

But... to answer your question... I think I'm the only one who really sees it for what it is. That's actually why I finally came in to see you. I realized that it wasn't just normal family bickering anymore, and nobody else seemed to notice what was really going on. They're so subtle about it... using the parish committee and the things they do up at the altar to push me out. They're doing it in a way where everyone else just thinks they're being devout, but I know they're doing it to make everyone forget all the things I've done for this family. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm repeating myself, and I really don't want to take up too much of your time with my family troubles. It just... it feels so isolating when you're the only one who sees it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too difficult or... or demanding of your sympathy. I just wanted to answer your question honestly.
How long have you felt like your in-laws are plotting against you?

Oh... um, let me think. I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is, I know every family has their little squabbles and I don't want to sound like I'm holding a grudge. I try so hard to be forgiving, I really do. 

But... well, this whole... crisis, I guess you could call it... it's been going on for about two months now. It all really started after we had this terrible fight over the Día de los Muertos altar. That's when things just felt different, like it shifted from a normal argument to... to them really trying to push me out. 

I feel so foolish even calling it a "crisis," I'm sure you hear about much worse things from other people all day long. I'm sorry to take up your time with something that started over an altar... does that sound terribly petty of me, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline like you asked.
Do you ever have times where you don't think your in-laws are plotting against you?

Oh... um... I really, really wish I could say yes to that. I try so hard to give them the benefit of the doubt, I honestly do. Sometimes I'll sit quietly and try to tell myself, maybe I'm just overreacting, or maybe it's just a simple misunderstanding. I hate the idea of assuming the worst about my own family, and I don't want you to think I'm inflexible or just holding onto anger. 

But... well, I know I keep coming back to this, and I am so sorry if I sound like a broken record... but no, the feeling doesn't really go away. Because, like I was saying, that's the whole reason I finally came in to see you. I just know in my heart that they aren't just arguing with me anymore. The things they are doing with the altar, and how they are using the parish committee... it's just always there. They are actively trying to push me out and make everyone completely forget everything I've done for this family. I try to shake it off and pretend everything is fine, but I can't, because I know it's what they're really doing. 

Does that make me sound terribly stubborn, Doctor? I'm trying my best to be objective, I really am, I just want to answer you truthfully.
Does your belief that your in-laws are plotting against you ever change or waver?

Oh, well... I know you just asked me something very similar, and I really hope I didn't misunderstand you the first time. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I don't want to seem like I'm being difficult or... or clinging to this idea just to be dramatic. I always try to see the good in people, especially family. 

But... no, it doesn't really waver. I wish it did. I've tried to tell myself I'm just being sensitive, but... that's exactly why I had to come see you. I just *know* they aren't just arguing with me anymore. It's not a misunderstanding. They are deliberately using the altar, and the parish committee, to push me out of the picture entirely. They want everyone to just... forget all the sacrifices I've made and everything I've done for this family over the years. 

I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. I just want to be completely honest with you about why I'm here. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it properly.
Do you think it's possible that your in-laws' actions are being misinterpreted by you?

Oh... um... I suppose... I mean, I really wish I could say yes. I know how important it is to keep an open mind, and I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or... or just looking for reasons to be upset. I try so hard to look at things from their perspective, I really do. 

But... well, I just can't see it any other way. I'm sorry to keep saying the same thing, I know it probably sounds like I'm not listening to you. But that's the whole reason I'm here. I just know, deep down, that they aren't just arguing with me. It's so clear to me how they're using the altar and turning the parish committee against me... they really are trying to push me out and erase everything I've done for them. 

I feel terrible saying it so bluntly, and I hope you don't think poorly of me for being so sure about something so awful. Does it make me sound unreasonable to say I don't think I'm misinterpreting it? I just want to be a good patient and give you the truth.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about your in-laws plotting against you?

Oh, doctor... I feel like I'm frustrating you, and I am so, so sorry. I know you're trying to help me see another side to this, and part of me just wants to say 'yes, of course I can change my mind' just so I'm giving you a better answer. I really want to be cooperative, I honestly do. 

But... I promised I would be completely honest with you. And the truth is... I can't change my mind, because it's not just in my head. Like I was trying to explain before, that's the whole reason I came in to get help. I know they aren't just having a normal family argument with me. They are actually using the altar, and getting the parish committee involved, to completely push me out of the picture. They want everyone to just forget all the good I've done for this family over the years. 

I feel awful that I can't give you the answer you're looking for. Am I being too difficult? I really, really hope you aren't upset with me. I just don't know how to pretend it isn't happening when it's so clear to me.
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your belief about your in-laws plotting against you?

Oh, dear... I feel like I'm failing a test here, and I really, really don't want to disappoint you. I know you're trying so hard to help me look at the facts differently, and I appreciate your patience with me so much. I'd love to say that if someone just showed me a piece of paper or some proof, I'd change my mind right away. I want to be a reasonable person for you, I truly do. 

But... well, I've already seen what's happening with my own eyes. That's the whole reason I came in to see you in the first place. I realized they weren't just arguing with me over normal family things. I really wish they were! But they're using the altar, and they've gotten the parish committee involved to just... push me out entirely. They want to make sure everyone forgets all the good things I've done for this family over the years. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm sounding like a broken record, repeating the same things to you again and again. I just don't know what evidence could possibly undo what they've already done at the church. Am I making any sense at all? I really hope I'm answering your questions the right way, doctor.
Do you think about your in-laws plotting against you all the time?

Oh... um, no, not all the time! I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over it every single minute of the day. I know that wouldn't be healthy, and I try very hard to stay busy and keep a positive attitude. I really do try to focus on other things, I promise.

But... well, it does come up a lot, I suppose. Especially when I think about the church. I mean, like I was saying, I came in because I realized it wasn't just a simple disagreement anymore. When I saw how they were using the altar... and getting the parish committee involved just to push me out and erase everything I've done for them... it's just hard to ignore something that big. 

I feel terrible bringing it up again, I know I must sound so negative. I really try not to dwell on it, but when they're actively doing these things, it's just... it's hard to get it out of my head. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound too fixated on it... I really am trying my best to handle this the right way.
Do you think your belief that your in-laws are plotting against you is based on facts or just a feeling you have?

Oh, doctor... I feel so silly because I know how it must sound to you. I really want to give you the answer that shows I'm being logical and reasonable. I know you're trying to help me separate my feelings from the facts, and I appreciate that so much. I'm trying very hard to do that, I promise. 

But... well, to me, it really is based on facts. I wouldn't have come in to get help if it was just a feeling, you know? I'm not the kind of person who just makes things up or gets hysterical over nothing. I realized it wasn't just them arguing with me... it's the actual things they are doing. Like using the altar, and... and getting the parish committee involved. That's real. They are doing those things to push me out and make everyone forget everything I've done for the family. 

I feel so bad, I feel like I'm frustrating you by sticking to this. I really don't mean to be difficult. It's just... it's what I know is happening. Am I being too stubborn? I really want to be doing this right, and I hope you can understand why it's so hard for me to just say it's only a feeling.
Do you think your belief about your in-laws plotting against you could be a mistaken idea?

Oh, goodness... I know I must be testing your patience, doctor. I really, really wish I could just nod and say yes, that it's all a big misunderstanding. I want to be a good patient for you, and I know saying it might be a mistake is probably what I should do. I don't want you to think I'm just this paranoid, stubborn old woman who won't listen to reason. 

But... well, it's just so hard to say it's a mistake when I've lived through it. Like I mentioned before, that's the whole reason I came in to see you. It wasn't just normal bickering. I realized they were actually using the altar, and they got the parish committee involved. And it's all just to push me out... to make everyone completely forget everything I've done for this family over the years. 

I'm so sorry, I feel terrible repeating myself. I know I must sound like a broken record, and I really don't want to disappoint you. It's just... how can it be a mistaken idea when they've gone to such lengths at the church? Am I making things too difficult for you by saying that? I really am trying to be helpful, doctor.
Do you think there's anything that could ever happen that would make you change your mind about your in-laws plotting against you?

Oh, doctor... I really wish I could say yes. I know that's the right answer, the healthy answer. I want to be open-minded, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being rigid or difficult. I'm trying so hard to be cooperative, I really am.

But... well, I just don't know what could possibly happen to change my mind at this point. I mean, I didn't want to believe it at first, either. But I came in to see you because I finally had to face the truth—that they weren't just arguing with me like normal families do. When they started using the altar... and getting the parish committee involved... it was so clear that they were actively trying to push me out. They want everyone to forget everything I've sacrificed and done for this family. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear. I feel like I'm failing this test, and I really hate letting you down. It's just... once you see them do something like that at the church, how can you unsee it? Does that make sense at all, or am I just sounding completely unreasonable? I really do want to get better, I promise.
Do you think that other people, outside of your family and the church, are also plotting against you?

Oh, goodness, no. No, doctor. I promise you, I don't think anything like that. I really hope you don't think I'm one of those people who believes the whole world is out to get them. I know how crazy that would sound, and I would never want you to think I've completely lost my grip on reality. 

I know I keep repeating myself, and I feel just awful taking up your time with the same story, but... well, it really is just my in-laws. Like I said, that's the only reason I came in to see you. It's just them taking things too far. It's just them using the altar and the parish committee to push me out and make sure everyone forgets what I've done for this family. 

It's strictly them. I don't suspect the neighbors or people at the grocery store or the mailman or anything like that. Does... does that help show that I'm still thinking clearly about everything else? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, and I hope it's a good sign that I know it's only my in-laws doing this.
Has there ever been a time when you didn't think your in-laws were plotting against you, even if it was just for a day?

Oh, well... I really want to say yes, doctor. I know it would probably make things simpler, and I'd love to tell you that there are days where everything feels perfectly fine and normal. I really don't want to come across as someone who just dwells on the negative all the time... I promise I try to be positive. 

But if I'm being completely honest—and I know I should be honest with you—ever since I realized what they were doing, it's just been there. Every day. I mean, how could I forget it? Like I've said, and I'm so sorry to keep bringing it up, but it's the whole reason I'm sitting here today. Once I figured out that this wasn't just normal family arguing... that they were actually using the altar and getting the parish committee involved just to push me out and erase everything I've done for them... well, you can't just turn that off for a day, you know? 

I really wish I could give you a better answer. I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or holding onto a grudge. I'm just trying to tell you exactly how it's been. Is it okay that I answered it that way? I'm really trying to do this right.
Do you think your belief about your in-laws plotting against you is something that only you understand, or do you think others would understand it if they knew all the facts?

Oh, I... I'd really like to think that if someone else knew all the facts, they would understand. I certainly hope so, anyway. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around making up wild stories that nobody else could possibly grasp. I try to be very reasonable, I really do. 

But, well, if another person saw exactly what was happening—if they saw how my in-laws weren't just having normal family arguments with me, but were actually... you know, using the altar... and getting the parish committee involved just to push me out and make sure everyone forgets everything I've done for this family... I think they would see it, too. 

I mean, like I've said, I came in here to see you because it became so undeniable, and I'd hope any fair-minded person would see it the exact same way if they had all the pieces in front of them. Does that make sense? I really hope I don't sound too defensive or stubborn when I say that. I just want you to know I'm trying to look at this logically. Am I answering your questions okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think your belief about your in-laws plotting against you is a delusion?

Oh, goodness, no. A delusion? Oh, I really hope you don't think I'm... well, that I'm crazy or anything like that. I know "delusion" is a very strong word, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just making things up in my head. I promise I'm not. I try very hard to stay grounded and sensible.

I know I've said it a few times now—and I really am sorry for repeating myself so much—but it's just the truth of why I came in to see you. I wouldn't be here if it was just regular family bickering. But it's not. I know for a fact they are using the altar, and they've gotten the parish committee involved, all just to push me out and make sure everyone forgets everything I've sacrificed and done for this family. 

It's really happening, doctor, I promise. I wouldn't waste your time with something I just imagined. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying it's real, I just want to be as honest and helpful as I can be.
